items.text: The documented direct/proposal distinction and policy representation trace to the person's operation/consequence scope, preserve the origin/undo/later-checking interface obligations, and retain the declared-checkpoint override. Verify REQ-001 through VER-001.

verification.text: Review the delivered contract and representation against SOW-074 and V4-HI-22/40/42; compare direct, proposal and declared-checkpoint cases against the recorded person-set scope, tracing origin/undo/later-checking responsibilities to the named consumers. Preserve the comparison and any missing consumer evidence.

items.text: The contract and semantic cases keep every subject in REQ-002 distinct: operation success and evidence of any one act do not establish another act; an independently evidenced act is not rejected solely for absent proposal acceptance; an agent-prepared decision alone is not recorded as the person's performance. A positive faithful-recording case preserves an actually performed human act with the human decision actor distinct from the agent recorder, without inventing recording permission or reserved-act authority. Verify through VER-002.

verification.text: Review and exercise semantic cases for proposal preparation, application success, agent examination, human checked mark, edit acceptance, engineering approval and professional reliance. For each, inspect actual actor/subject/evidence and check that absence of another act neither creates that act nor alone invalidates the independently supported one. Include a positive case faithfully recording an actually performed human act, with the human decision actor distinct from the agent recorder, alongside fabricated human attribution and operation-success-only negative cases; compare to the current V4-AUT-03/V4-HI-31 and accepted HTML-D03 basis cited by REQ-002 and retain exact fixture/result references. The recording case supplies no new recording permission or reserved-act policy.

items.text: Agent-output cases carry none of the professional standing prohibited by REQ-003, while a separately evidenced professional act remains attributed only to its actual actor and subject. Verify through VER-003.

verification.text: Inspect agent-output and separately evidenced professional-act cases against V4-AUT-05; compare displayed/recorded standing to actual evidence and confirm that agent success, checking and acceptance confer no certification, sealing, professional approval or code-compliance claim.

items.text: For a concretely adopted reserved act, embedded and external agent attempts cannot establish its performance or attribution to the person; unresolved operations identify the applicable OI-001/OI-002 decision, owner and point of need without a guessed policy value or dependent implementation claim. Verify REQ-004 through VER-004.

verification.text: Compare each adopted reserved-act case with its actual policy decision and inspect embedded/external enforcement conformance evidence from the responsible implementation. For each unruled case, inspect the OI-001/OI-002 owner and point-of-need hold; record absent decisions or host evidence as unresolved, not as a passed behavior or a new policy choice.

items.text: All proposal-decision wording in the delivered contract, configuration examples and semantic fixtures uses "accept" for edit acceptance and does not relabel it engineering approval. Verify REQ-005 through VER-005.

verification.text: Inspect proposal-decision language in the delivered document, configuration examples and fixtures against V4-HI-33; retain locations showing "accept" and findings for any proposal label that implies engineering approval.

items.text: The shared default contract and policy examples preserve conservative consequential-operation defaults and SWB row, multi-row and batch proposal acceptance; person-granted widening remains bounded by the adopted reserved policy and checkpoints. Verify REQ-006 through VER-006.

verification.text: Compare contract and policy cases with V4-HI-41/42/51: consequential-operation conservative defaults, SWB model-change proposal defaults, row/multi-row/batch acceptance, and person-granted widening constrained by adopted reserved acts and declared checkpoints. Identify which observations are local contract evidence and which require host conformance evidence.

items.text: OUT-002 accounts for each concrete policy value it carries with its adopted decision basis and consuming responsibility, marks still-open values explicitly, and supplies no inferred always-reserved list or classifier treatment. Verify REQ-001 and REQ-004 through VER-007.

verification.text: Trace each represented concrete policy value to its actual adopted decision, operation/consequence meaning and named consumer. Compare unresolved entries to OI-001/OI-002 and confirm they select neither a global list nor classifier behavior. Review representation completeness against the adopted cases without inventing values for open cases.

items.text: The delivered contract's boundary accounting assigns every excluded act in REQ-007 to its cited owner, keeps local/shared commitments included, and does not claim host implementation, external evidence, adoption or any person's act merely from this contract's existence. Verify through VER-008.

verification.text: Compare the act-by-act boundary in REQ-007 with CLM-002 through CLM-005 and their accepted source rows; verify that local/shared policy definition and receiving work remain included while sibling production, external implementation, policy adoption and actual human/professional acts retain their owners. Record any ownership mismatch and unsupported external completion claim.

items.text: OUT-003 covers the source-grounded reserved-act and semantic-label obligations in REQ-002 through REQ-006 with identified fixtures and actual candidate-bound results; unresolved policy cases are reported as awaiting their decision instead of being counted as passing implemented behavior. Verify through VER-009.

verification.text: Review the fixture set against REQ-002 through REQ-006, run applicable fixtures against the identified candidate, and retain fixture IDs, candidate identity, actual results and limits. Reconcile coverage with the matrix; distinguish unresolved policy cases and absent host evidence from passing local fixtures. A fixture expectation cannot decide OI-001/OI-002 or establish a human act.
